source.title: Robust Robotic Control from Pixels using Contrastive Recurrent State-Space Models

confidence_rationale: Contrastive losses on the next-state prediction explicitly pull together (s_t, a_t) -> s_{t+1} pairs and push apart distractors. This is structurally the right inductive bias for preserving per-action divergence -- you cannot solve the contrastive task if K different actions all map to the same predicted z. Direct ML evidence for the kind of training objective option (ii) would use. Workshop venue and lack of explicit per-action-distinguishability metrics knock confidence down somewhat.
failure_signatures: Reconstruction-based latent dynamics losses (the standard RSSM objective) are agnostic to whether actions are distinguishable in the predicted latent -- they only require pixel reconstruction; the contrastive alternative directly penalises action-conditional indistinguishability.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Replacing the standard RSSM reconstruction loss with a contrastive prediction loss yields more robust pixel control because contrastive learning forces the latent to preserve action-relevant distinctions that pixel-reconstruction does not require.
mapping.ree_translation: E2's training loss in REE-v3 is reconstruction-shaped (predict next z_world). Reconstruction losses do not, in general, penalise the model for representing K different actions identically -- if the action effect is small relative to the state's autoregressive dynamics, gradient descent finds the trivial solution. A contrastive next-state loss conditioned on action would directly penalise the failure surfaced in V3-EXQ-571.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper is a workshop submission and does not report a per-action distinguishability metric directly; the inference that contrastive losses prevent K-action collapse is structural rather than empirical. Also, contrastive RSSM in the paper is paired with pixel observations; REE-v3's E2 operates on a learned z_gamma latent, so the negative-sample distribution would have to be redesigned to be informative. CROSS-REFERENCED FOR MECH-520 2026-08-26 (not re-pulled -- see targeted_review_mech_520 for the dedicated pull): this paper's core structural claim, that reconstruction-shaped losses are agnostic to action-conditional collapse while a contrastive alternative is not, is a k=1 instance (single-axis: action identity) of MECH-520's general claim that value/reconstruction-shaped objectives admit representational collapse and a cross-prediction constraint resists it. It supports MECH-520 only at that narrow scope: this paper never argues for or tests a general VALUE-carving objective (it compares reconstruction vs. contrastive, not value vs. predictive), and per targeted_review_mech_520's Tang et al. (2023) entry, even a predictive/contrastive-shaped constraint is not automatically anti-collapse without the right optimization dynamics -- a qualification this workshop paper does not address.
mapping.source_context: Vision-based robotic control with distractor environments; comparison against reconstruction-based RSSM baselines.

confidence_components.notes: Apple workshop paper; methodologically sound but light on direct per-action analysis. Strong structural argument but no smoking-gun quantitative result for our specific failure mode.
